title: Hot Tokens
hints: How many times does each token appear? Which structure answers that in one pass?
You need the k best by (count, then smaller id). Sorting every distinct token works; can you keep only k of them?
Count with a hash map, then keep a min-heap of size k ordered by (count asc, id desc) so the weakest candidate is on top.

wrong.tie_larger_first.cpp: breaks ties by larger token id instead of smaller
wrong.tle_quadratic.cpp: counts with a linear scan per token (quadratic, fails the perf group)

strategy.question: Scout the statement: which plan fits n up to 2*10^5 and 'k most frequent, ties by smaller id'?
options: Count each token with a linear scan over the others, then sort
Hash-map the counts, then sort or heap-select by (count desc, id asc)
Sort the log once and use binary search per query
Keep an array indexed by token id
strategy.why: Counting in a hash map is O(n); selecting the top k by sort (O(d log d)) or a size-k heap (O(d log k)) is fast. A per-token scan is O(n^2) and fails the perf tests; ids reach 10^9, so a direct-index array is far too large.
